## Overview
### Introduction to Google: Nano Banana 2
The Google: Nano Banana 2 (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image Preview) model, released by Google on 2024-01-01, is a standard-tier, non-open-source language model designed for a variety of natural language processing tasks. This model is part of the Gemini series and is specifically designated as version 3.1 Flash Image Preview. With its robust architecture, it supports capabilities such as text processing, function calling, JSON mode, streaming, and structured outputs, making it versatile for developers.

### Architecture and Strengths
Google: Nano Banana 2 boasts a context window of 65,536 tokens and can generate outputs of up to 65,536 tokens, providing a comprehensive framework for handling extensive and complex inputs. Its knowledge cutoff is 2023-12, ensuring that it is informed by data up to that point. The model's strengths are reflected in its benchmark scores, including an MMLU score of 80.0 and an LMSYS Arena ELO of 1200, indicating its proficiency in understanding and generating human-like text. Its pricing structure, with input costs at $0.5 per 1M tokens and output costs at $3.0 per 1M tokens, positions it as a competitive option for developers looking for a balance between cost and performance.

### Use Cases and Cost Considerations
The Google: Nano Banana 2 model is best suited for applications such as chat, text generation, coding, analysis, RAG pipelines, and summarization, thanks to its diverse capabilities. Developers can expect to pay $0.0018 for 1,000 calls averaging 500 tokens, scaling to $0.018 for 10,000 calls and $0.18 for 100,000 calls, making it an accessible choice for a wide range of projects.
